MEASURED 2026-11-27 (retraction): worker_threads is NOT an engine limitation — the engine ships a real Worker (mbjs-libc.c, compiled with USE_WORKER) exported from mbjs:os. It creates a new runtime+context with a message-pipe pair and loads the named module in the worker. Worker.parent is set inside the worker, so isMainThread/parentPort are DETECTED, not hardcoded. Round trip verified in selftest/mochi-worker.js: parent posts {n:10}, worker computes 10! and posts back {fact:3628800}, parent's 'message' handler receives it, worker reports isMainThread false. Terminate via timer-scheduled promise. Measured limitation: after a Worker is created the host process never exits on its own (no JS-visible exit API), so the selftest reports by printing WORKER_ALL_OK and the harness applies `timeout`. Residual honest limits: no terminate handle, threadId null, workerData not delivered, no 'error' event.
